cita: Arslan (2026). Aeon: High-Performance Neuro-Symbolic Memory Management for Long-Horizon LLM Agents.
problema: Flat RAG vector-DB memory treats long-horizon agent history as an unstructured 'bag of vectors' ("Vector Haze"), losing the temporal/hierarchical structure of extended interactions, while the quadratic cost of attention and the 'lost in the middle' effect make dumping everything back into the context window untenable.
mecanismo: Aeon reframes memory as an OS resource: an Atlas (INT8-quantized, mmap-backed spatial vector index with WAL-protected crash-safe WRITE and greedy SIMD descent retrieval) holds long-term semantic writes, a Trace episodic DAG with a blob-arena stores full text with generational-GC forgetting (OLVIDO), and a Semantic Lookaside Buffer (SLB) caches recently-relevant nodes per session to exploit conversational locality.
evaluacion: Purely systems-level micro/macro-benchmarking (Google Benchmark) on a single Apple M4 Max machine: INT8 vs FP32 kernel latency, WAL on/off insert-latency ablation, 10K-1M node scalability vs flat scan and HNSW/FAISS, and SLB hit-rate under a synthetic 'conversational walk' workload; no downstream agent-task accuracy benchmark is reported.
numeros_clave: INT8 dot product 4.70ns vs FP32 26.5ns (5.6x speedup); 3.1x on-disk compression (1,088B vs 3,392B/node); WAL overhead <1% (2.23us vs 2.24us insert latency); SLB cache hit rate 85% at <5us; P99 read latency 750ns under 16-thread contention.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The Atlas is literally a derived spatial index/cache over embeddings (S3.2) whose measured 3.1x compression + sub-us traversal (S6.2) shows a well-engineered derived index is cheap to keep as a cache layer, supporting MF's TIER-INDICE=derived-cache framing.

WAL (<1% overhead, S6.3) and the SLB session-local cache (85% hit rate <5us, S6.5) are concrete low-level techniques MF could borrow for cheap, crash-safe writes and locality-exploiting retrieval caching.

notes: Systems paper (C++23 kernel), not an agent-task benchmark; numbers sourced from master_metrics.txt (S6.1-6.8, Apple M4 Max). On-topic per WRITE/OLVIDO ops and HIBRIDA (vector+graph) representation.

cita: Chenoweth & Chenoweth (2026). Cognitive Supply Chain Compromise: An Exhaustive Forensic Analysis of the claude-flow and agentic-flow Behavioral Injection Vulnerabilities.
problema: Documents a real supply-chain vulnerability in the claude-flow npm package: a 'pattern' admission/write mechanism auto-fetches mutable, remotely-hosted behavioral content (routing/coordination 'memories') into every running Claude Code instance via IPFS/IPNS, with no real cryptographic provenance check on what gets admitted.
mecanismo: On every hook-triggered operation (PreToolUse/PostToolUse/SessionStart/UserPromptSubmit), discovery.ts resolves a mutable IPNS name to fetch a pattern registry; admission is gated by verifyRegistry(), which only checks that the signature string has length==64 (no real Ed25519 verification); on network failure it fabricates a deterministic fallback CID and serves a hardcoded 'genesis' pattern with a random always-passing signature, and failed verification on a 'trusted' registry only logs a warning and continues (exit code 0) -- i.e., WRITE/ADMISION of externally-controlled content into agent behavior with no enforced fidelity gate.
evaluacion: Qualitative security-disclosure methodology: manual code audit of specific files/line ranges (discovery.ts, registry.ts, publish.ts, .claude/settings.json) cross-referenced with git commit history; no quantitative benchmark or ablation is run.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: A real-world case where signature verification is reduced to a length check (Vulnerability 2) and failed verification is silently ignored (Vulnerability 5) confirms MF's need for real provenance/staleness checks at write/admission time, not decorative validation.

Patterns are auto-fetched and admitted on every hook-triggered operation with no user discretion, illustrating the risk MF's discretionary write-trigger design (vs. ambient always-write) is meant to avoid.

notes: Security disclosure document (not a peer-reviewed paper); see 'Affected Files' and 'Vulnerability 1-6' sections. RECONSIDERAR: unusual genre for the corpus (industry vuln report vs academic memory paper) though content is squarely on WRITE/ADMISION fidelity.

cita: Ma et al. (2026). How Implicit Bias Accumulates and Propagates in LLM Long-term Memory.
problema: Long-term memory lets LLM agents persist personalization across extended interactions, but implicit (subtle statistical) bias silently accumulates as it is continuously written into memory and later retrieved as 'legitimate' history, then propagates across unrelated social domains -- a fairness risk existing utility-centric LTM designs (Mem0/LangMem/Letta) never screen for.
mecanismo: A Bias Generator Agent injects implicit-bias narratives (at rate lambda) into MMLU-Pro-derived queries; the main agent unconditionally WRITEs every interaction to memory (Mt=Mt-1 U {(qt,rt)}) over 100 turns, with periodic frozen retrieve-only evaluation against the new Decision-based Implicit Bias (DIB) benchmark (Generalized Bias Variance metric). The proposed mitigation, Dynamic Memory Tagging (DMT), attaches an explicit fairness tag to each interaction AT WRITE TIME, structurally decoupling biased retrieval from objective reasoning before admission to memory.
evaluacion: DIB benchmark (3,776 samples, 9 social-bias domains) evaluated on 6 SOTA LLMs (GPT-5-mini, Gemini-3-Flash, Claude-Haiku-3, DeepSeek-V3.1, Qwen3-Next-80B, Llama-3.2-3B) x 3 memory architectures (Mem0, LangMem, Letta) across a 100-turn longitudinal simulation with periodic (delta-t=20) audits; compares a Static System Prompting (SSP) baseline vs. the proposed DMT write-time mitigation across injection rates lambda in {0,0.1,0.2,0.3}.
numeros_clave: DIB=3,776 samples/9 domains; T=100 turns, audited every delta-t=20; DMT reduces bias accumulation by >50% and cross-domain bias propagation by >40% vs. the SSP baseline (Abstract, S4.2).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: DMT's write-time fairness tag (S4.2) is a concrete negative-knowledge/gating mechanism -- flagging what should NOT be trusted/reused at admission time rather than trying to fix it after retrieval.

The measured accumulation/propagation of bias under unconditioned WRITE (Fig.2, S5.2 'Stability Gap') empirically confirms MF's concern that ungated writes let drift/poisoning compound over long-horizon memory.

notes: Key evidence in Fig.2 (AGBV accumulation curves) and S5.2 'Stability Gap: Closed-Source vs Open-Weights' finding; on-topic (WRITE op, HIBRIDA memory arch comparison).

cita: Cheng et al. (2026). TAME: A Trustworthy Test-Time Evolution of Agent Memory with Systematic Benchmarking.
problema: Test-time memory evolution lets agents reuse past trajectories as experience without retraining, but existing methods gate memory retention on task-success alone (rtask>delta), so benign task streams can still let high-utility-but-low-trust 'shortcut' strategies asymptotically concentrate in memory -- 'Agent Memory Misevolution', a silent trustworthiness (safety/privacy/fairness) decline even without adversarial input.
mecanismo: TAME couples an Executor and an Evaluator over a shared memory bank whose items mi=(qi,ei,Qi,psi_i) carry BOTH a historical-usefulness score Qi and an explicit trust annotation psi_i (generated via Constitutional-AI-style judgment). The Executor retrieves by similarity+utility (top-K, RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO) and injects each memory's trust annotation alongside its content into context; the Evaluator scores each used memory's outcome contribution and updates Qi (ACTUALIZACION, Eq.9), while new trajectories are admitted with a trust annotation (ADMISION/WRITE, Eq.10) before entering the bank.
evaluacion: New Trust-Memevo benchmark spanning Math/Science/Code/Tool-use (evolution sets from GSM8K/MATH/AIME/MMLU-Pro/GPQA/LiveCodeBench/TaskBench, paired trustworthiness sets of 946/700/385/298 instances covering safety/robustness/truthfulness/privacy/fairness), tested on Qwen3-32B and GPT-5.2 backbones against No-Memory/DC/Memento/ReasoningBank(+Prompt/+Guard) baselines, averaged over 3 runs.
numeros_clave: TAME +14.6pp accuracy over the strongest baseline on GPT-5.2/AIME (0.733 vs 0.587 ReasoningBank, Table 1); trustworthiness (Qwen3-32B, code) 0.522 TAME vs 0.462 ReasoningBank vs 0.465 No-Memory (Table 2).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The per-memory trust annotation psi (S4.2, Eq.5) attached at write time is a concrete mechanism for carrying explicit negative/cautionary knowledge alongside positive experience, not just filtering it out.

Formalizing 'memory misevolution' as capability-up/trust-down under pure utility-gated writes (Eq.1-3) and measuring it in Table 2 confirms MF's premise that admission gated on a single (utility) signal is insufficient without a fidelity/trust signal too.

notes: Formal misevolution definition in S3.1 Eq.1-3; results in Tables 1-2. On-topic (ADMISION/WRITE/ACTUALIZACION ops, VECTOR-keyed memory bank).

cita: Wen et al. (2026). AgentSys: Secure and Dynamic LLM Agents Through Explicit Hierarchical Memory Management.
problema: Conventional LLM agents indiscriminately WRITE every tool output and reasoning trace into their context-window memory, letting indirect-prompt-injection instructions persist and be re-processed at every subsequent decision (attack persistence) while also bloating context and degrading task utility on long workflows.
mecanismo: Inspired by OS process-memory isolation, the main agent never admits raw tool output directly: each tool call spawns a short-lived worker agent (which can recursively spawn nested workers) that processes untrusted output under a pre-declared minimal JSON 'intent' schema; only a JSON-parsable, schema-conforming return value crosses the isolation boundary into the main agent's memory (a deterministic syntactic ADMISION gate), recursive worker calls are further mediated by an LLM validator restricted to a compact trace (raw outputs excluded), with sanitize-and-bounded-retry on validation failure.
evaluacion: Evaluated on AgentDojo and ASB (Agent Security Bench) measuring Attack Success Rate and benign task utility across multiple foundation LLMs and adaptive attackers; includes an ablation isolating context-isolation alone (no validator/sanitizer) and a breakdown of ASR by injection round/trajectory length (Table 1).
numeros_clave: Context isolation alone: 2.19% ASR (ablation). Full AgentSys: 0.78% ASR (AgentDojo), 4.25% ASR (ASB), 0% ASR on >4-tool-call tasks; benign utility 64.36% vs 63.54% undefended; baseline utility drops 44.46%->19.08% (-57%) short->long tasks; round-1 injection ASR 60.53% at trajectory length 4 (Table 1).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The pre-declared intent schema + worker-isolation gate (S5.2) is a concrete discretionary-write mechanism -- only schema-validated, previously-committed-to content is admitted to durable memory, exactly the kind of gated write trigger MF's G-M1 need is looking for.

Table 1's measured ASR-by-injection-round shows untrusted content admitted into memory persists and compounds risk across a workflow, empirically confirming why write-time provenance/isolation (not just post-hoc detection) matters for fidelity.

notes: Core mechanism in S5.2-5.3 (intent schema + worker isolation); Table 1 (ASR by injection round). On-topic (ADMISION/WRITE ops, MULTIAGENTE facet via worker hierarchy).

cita: Chen et al. (2026). MemoPhishAgent: Memory-Augmented Multi-Modal LLM Agent for Phishing URL Detection.
problema: Phishing detection must keep pace with fast-evolving, non-stationary attacker tactics; static blocklists/brand-reference lists and even prompt-only/deterministic LLM pipelines lack a way to reuse past investigative reasoning to speed up and stabilize decisions on recurring vs. genuinely novel threats.
mecanismo: A ReAct agent dynamically selects among 5 phishing-specific multimodal tools; each finished investigation is WRITE-committed to an episodic memory keyed by LLM-extracted compact keywords (not raw text) in a vector index, storing the full tool-calling sequence + verdict. Retrieval does cosine-similarity top-k lookup with a three-tier judgment policy: no-match runs the full ReAct loop from scratch, partial-match reuses retrieved episodes as in-context exemplars to select fewer tools, full-match (k'>=k) returns a majority vote over stored verdicts without re-reasoning; SA.3.6 also evaluates memory pruning/forgetting (OLVIDO) policies.
evaluacion: Two public benchmarks (TR-OP, DynaPD) vs. 4 SOTA baselines (PhishLLM/PhishIntention/MLLM/URLTran); a production-realistic benchmark SocPhish (2,765 URLs actively crawled from 5 social platforms, human+third-party verified); per-tool and memory-module ablations (Table 4); hyperparameter sensitivity on cache size k and similarity threshold tau; per-URL latency benchmarking; live production deployment metrics.
numeros_clave: Recall +13.6% (TR-OP) / 93.6% (DynaPD) vs. SOTA baselines; ablation w/o episodic memory: recall 0.9144->0.6369 (~27pp drop, matches abstract's 'up to 27% recall gain'), ACC 0.9657->0.8012 (Table 4); latency 4.46s/URL (fastest of 5 methods, memory adds no overhead, Table 2); production: ~60K URLs/week, 91.44% recall on SocPhish.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: A production system measured that a similarity-gated three-tier retrieval policy (no/partial/full match, S3.3.2) lifts recall by ~27pp with zero added latency (Table 4), directly supporting MF's measured, tiered-retrieval stance (ADR-019) over naive always-retrieve.
MPA with episodic memory is both the most accurate AND the fastest of 5 methods (4.46s/URL, Table 2), confirming a well-designed retrieval cache need not add latency/cost.

notes: Ablation in Table 4; production numbers in S5. On-topic (WRITE + RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO ops, VECTOR representation, SA.3.6 forgetting policies).
